title: Prometheus histogram reset caused SLO burn alert — retro & mitigation notes
content:
Summary:

On 2025-02-09 22:18 UTC we saw a rapid SLO burn alert for the "api-latency" objective for Hosted API (99th p95/p99 window). The alerting pipeline fired repeatedly over ~40m and paged oncall. Impact: transient customer-facing latency regression reports and noise in the oncall rotation (4 pages).

Observed behavior that made this incident unusual:
- The SLO calculation query returned a sudden jump in error budget burn even though request latencies at the edge (nginx access logs) did not show a corresponding spike in request duration.
- Prometheus metrics for request duration histograms showed a reset/zeroing of the _sum and _count for several histogram series during a rotate of the exporter process, but buckets remained populated for a short period.
- Our SLO query uses increase(api_request_duration_seconds_sum[5m]) / increase(api_request_duration_seconds_count[5m]) pattern to compute moving averages for threshold checks. When _sum/_count reset, the increase() returns unexpectedly large values (due to counter resets handling) which our alerting rules did not reliably account for in all cases, producing inflated p99 estimates.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2025-02-09 22:16: exporter rollout started in staging -> prod via automation (monitoring-agent v1.7.3).
- 22:18: first SLO burn alert fires.
- 22:20–22:40: alert repeats every evaluation cycle (1m). Oncall escalations at 22:22 and 22:30.
- 22:25: SRE oncall (Aisha) inspects Prometheus targets and sees exporter restarts on a subset of pods in the api autoscaling group.
- 22:27: Temporary silence added to reduce pager storm (mute for alert: slo-burn-high) while investigation ongoing.
- 22:35: Patch rolled to exporter to handle histogram metric export ordering (fix in PR linked).
- 22:50: Verify SLO query stable, unmute alert.
- 23:10: Post-incident notes begin.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed):
1) exporter (monitoring-agent v1.7.3) rolled and restarted processes in a way that exported histogram bucket series before the corresponding _sum/_count series were fully initialized, resulting in partial metric sets being visible to Prometheus during scrape windows.
2) Our SLO query relies on increase() over sum and count; increase() is sensitive to counter resets and needs robust reset-detection logic to avoid transient spikes. An exporter-side ordering problem plus the naive use of increase() produced anomalous numerator/denominator pairs that magnified apparent latency.

Why alerts fired / alert rule gap:
- The SLO alert rule uses a threshold on computed p99 derived from the ratio of increase(sum) / increase(count) and lacks a guard for very small denominator increases or suspected resets (e.g., ignore if increase(count) < X or treat large relative increases as resets).
- We do have a `prometheus_histogram_resets_total` metric in some exporters but not consistently across versions; our alerting rules did not reference it.

Immediate mitigations taken during incident:
- Muted the slo-burn alert to stop repeated paging while a targeted mitigation was validated.
- Rolled back the exporter to previous stable version in one AZ while QA validated fix.
- Deployed a hotfix to the exporter (ordering + zero-init) and restarted workloads behind a gradual rollout.
- Validated SLO queries over multiple sliding windows and cross-checked with raw nginx logs.

Longer-term fixes and action items (owner, ETA):
- Add guard clauses to SLO PromQL queries to skip evaluations when increase(count[5m]) < 50 (tunable) to avoid division by small numbers. (owner: Rachel Kim, ETA: 2025-02-21)
- Update alert rule to detect counter resets: use reset-aware functions and/or `resets()` as additional signal to suppress alerts during series churn. (owner: Carlos Mendez, ETA: 2025-02-18)
- Add exporter integration test: verify histogram _sum/_count ordering and zero-init under restart conditions. (owner: Tom Nguyen, ETA: 2025-02-28)
- Instrument the exporter to emit `exporter_init_complete` event metric — add to service discovery for Prometheus and pause SLO evaluations for targets with no init metric for X sec. (owner: Monitoring team, ETA: 2025-03-07)
- Dashboarding: create a small panel for "same-target bucket vs sum/count drift" to quickly triage histogram inconsistencies. (owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 2025-02-17)
- Runbook update: add a troubleshooting checklist for histogram-based SLOs that includes steps to check exporter restarts, delta on sum/count, and cross-check with raw request logs. (owner: eng-sre runbooks, ETA: 2025-02-16)

Runbook draft excerpt (to be added to /runbooks/histogram-slo-troubleshooting):
1) When an SLO burn alert fires for histogram-derived metrics:
  - Check `increase(<metric>_count[5m])` value. If < 50, suspect sampling/reset.
  - Query `resets(<metric>_count[5m])` and `increase(<metric>_count[5m])` side-by-side.
  - Look for exporter restart events in `kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total` for targets.
  - Cross-check with raw access logs for latency at the same timestamps.
  - If exporter ordering suspected, apply a temporary mute for the SLO alert and follow deployment rollback/hotfix process.

Example PromQL snippets (working):
- Count guard: `increase(api_request_duration_seconds_count[5m]) > 50`
- Reset-aware ratio: `sum(increase(api_request_duration_seconds_sum[5m])) / sum(increase(api_request_duration_seconds_count[5m]))` WITH additional `unless` when resets() > 0 for the same range.
- Simple suppression: `unless (resets(api_request_duration_seconds_count[5m]) > 0)` (note: tests required across Prometheus versions).

Post-incident notes on alerts and noise policy:
- Our current noise policy mutes alerts for 15m by default when incidents are investigated; that was useful here but we need faster diagnostics to avoid mute reliance.
- Consider a second-tier "suppress noisy SLOs on metric churn" automation that auto-mutes SLO alerts for a target when exporter restarts > N in 5m. This must have guardrails to avoid masking real incidents. (proposal owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 2025-03-01)

Open questions / unresolved items:
- What is the correct threshold for `increase(count)` guard for our traffic profiles? Need histograms of per-target counts to set a safe default. (action: generate distribution; owner: data-team, ETA: 2025-02-17)
- Can we standardize an `exporter_ready` metric across our fleet so alert rules can gate on it? (discussion needed with platform infra.)

Appendix: quick commands used during investigation:
- Prometheus query: `sum(increase(api_request_duration_seconds_sum[5m])) by (job,instance)`
- Check resets: `resets(api_request_duration_seconds_count[5m]) by (job,instance)`
- Check exporter restarts: `sum(increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{container=~"monitoring-agent.*"}[10m])) by (pod)`
- Cross-check nginx logs (example): `grep "200" /var/log/nginx/access.log | awk '{print $4,$7,$10}' | sed -n '...'`

Notes to self: this incident is an example of metric-semantic fragility — the math in alerts assumes stable metric shapes and exporter behavior. We should codify a short checklist for any SLO that depends on derived metrics (histograms, client-side counters, remote sampling).

Status: this is a working draft for the SRE runbooks page and will be converted to a formal postmortem if the action items have owners and dates confirmed.
